messages:
Sophie: Quick sync on onboarding gptj-ext-v1 into Dedicated. Weights are at s3://redwood-models/private/gpt-j-ext/v1/weights.tar.gz. Need to validate max context, kv cache format, and memory sizing before we flip routing.
Ajay: Got it. Any tokenizer quirks we should watch for?
Sophie: Yes 92 tokenizer is byte-level BPE and it doesn't define a BOS token. Training used an implicit BOS at position 0; our serving code expects `bos_id=1`. We can either set `add_bos=true` in tokenizer config or patch the serving mapping.
Kevin: What's our target max context? Model card claims 65,536 but some rotary components were originally 4k-based.
Sophie: Model card reports max_ctx=65536 but there may be rotor/base tuning for longer contexts. We need a KV memory sweep to see linear scaling and OOM boundaries.
Maria: I'll run the mem estimator. Command I plan to use:
```
python tools/mem_estimate.py \n  --model-path s3://redwood-models/private/gpt-j-ext/v1/weights.tar.gz \n  --dtype fp16 --batch 1 \n  --max-seq 65536 --warmup 1024
```
Expect outputs like:
```
seq=4096  mem_gpu=12.3GB  kv_bytes=4.1GB
seq=16384 mem_gpu=42.0GB  kv_bytes=16.4GB
seq=65536 mem_gpu=165.5GB kv_bytes=65.6GB  <-- likely OOM on single 80GB card
```
Ajay: Those numbers track with our back-of-envelope. For Dedicated we aim to keep per-replica under ~60GB to hit 75% of an 80GB card. 65k needs sharding or aggressive quantization/offload.
Kevin: What KV cache formats do we support? Need exact layout so I can validate loader code (interleaved per-head vs contiguous per-layer).
Sophie: Runtime supports `kv_flat_v1` (contiguous per-layer) and `kv_interleaved_v2` (per-head interleaved). The onboarding manifest left `kv_format: auto` and the host selected `kv_interleaved_v2`. I recommend pinning explicitly.
Ajay: Pinning to `kv_flat_v1` is safer for fallbacks, albeit slightly larger memory. For a canary we should test both.
Maria: I'll run the estimator matrix for both formats and seq lengths 16k and 65k, then share numbers here.
infra-bot: build:artifact-check passed for s3://redwood-models/private/gpt-j-ext/v1/weights.tar.gz (sha256: a3f2...)
Kevin: Also check tokenizer padding id. If `pad_token_id` != 0, we've seen shifted KV indices (pad=50256 caused issues in the past).
Sophie: Tokenizer config in S3 shows `pad_token: null` and `eos_token: 50256`. Let's explicitly set `padding_side: right` and `pad_token: 0` in the serving manifest to avoid surprises.
Ajay: For the memory strategy options we have:
- require multi-GPU sharding (TP/kv-shard)
- enable quantization (INT8/4bit) plus fused kernels
- enable prefix/KV offload for long sequences
My preference for a quick canary: quantize + `kv_flat_v1` on a 4x A100-80GB pool. Cheaper and faster than implementing sharded runtime.
Sophie: Agreed. Action items:
- @Maria: run estimations for seq=16k/65k and kv formats `kv_flat_v1`/`kv_interleaved_v2`, post results (ETA ~2h)
- @Ajay: prepare canary serving config with `pad_token=0`, `add_bos=true`, `kv_format=kv_flat_v1`, `quant=fp16`, and fallback to interleaved
- @Kevin: validate tokenizer/pad/eos changes won't break downstream eval harness
- @Sophie: I'll update model card with weights path, the tokenizer note, and a caveat about max_ctx
Maria: Kicking off runs now, will post outputs as soon as they finish.
Kevin: I'll queue quick smoke runs at 2k/8k once Maria posts mem numbers.
Ajay: Ping me when mem outputs are posted and I'll provision a 4x A100 canary.
Sophie: Keeping routing OFF for this model until canary passes. :lock:
